decision.summary: The Federal Reserve lowered the target range for the federal funds rate by 100 basis points to 0 to 1/4 percent.

changes.quote: The coronavirus outbreak has harmed communities and disrupted economic activity in many countries, including the United States.
changes.explanation: The Fed added this language to explicitly acknowledge the sudden health and economic disruptions caused by the coronavirus pandemic globally and domestically.

changes.quote: Available economic data show that the U.S. economy came into this challenging period on a strong footing.
changes.explanation: The Committee noted that solid prior economic data provided a strong baseline before the pandemic shock took hold.

changes.quote: The effects of the coronavirus will weigh on economic activity in the near term and pose risks to the economic outlook.
changes.explanation: This points out that the coronavirus creates immediate downward pressure and uncertainty for future economic growth.

changes.quote: In light of these developments, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 0 to 1/4 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed slashed interest rates drastically down to near zero to buffer the economy against the coronavirus shock.

tone_quotes.quote: The coronavirus outbreak has harmed communities and disrupted economic activity in many countries, including the United States.
The effects of the coronavirus will weigh on economic activity in the near term and pose risks to the economic outlook.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 14.87% APR, a 100 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $4.17.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 0.94% and moved -21 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.29% would fall by about $34.42 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $60.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 3.5%, and employers added an average of 209k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.3% over the past year (February 2020); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.7%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.8% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -13 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -11.98%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.41% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Federal Reserve will maintain this target range until it is confident that the economy has weathered recent events and is on track to achieve its maximum employment and price stability goals. The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 36%, cut 13%, hike 52% (educational purpose).
